source_text: Indeed, here's a fun and meaningful project: the R-nodes themselves could be presented as a cascade in exactly the sense we have been talking about and moreover with our admittedly quite complex pop-out wiring diagram in futon7a/about.html we have a "prototype" of such.  But in fact it's an elaborated prototype, i.e., a "wiring diagram" rather than merely a cascade.  So the cascade version would be a simplification of the elaborated wiring diagram.

fragments.text: Indeed, here's a fun and meaningful project: the R-nodes themselves could be presented as a cascade in exactly the sense we have been talking about and moreover with our admittedly quite complex pop-out wiring diagram in futon7a/about.html we have a "prototype" of such.
But in fact it's an elaborated prototype,
i.e., a "wiring diagram" rather than merely a cascade.
So the cascade version would be a simplification of the elaborated wiring diagram.

reply_text:
㊥ (gist) Yes — and the data already says what the simplification is. The harness figure is drawn from `p4ng/empirics-futon/aif-lean-dag.edn`: 17 drawn nodes, 43 edges, each edge a named Lean term (`o`, `mu`, `G`, `pi`, `C-tau`, `A`, `B`, …) with a class (23 imported, 10 absent, 6 present-not-imported, 1 unplaced). Those edges are already "what each step needs", carrying a token — the cascade's descent edge. What the wiring diagram has that a cascade cannot is a *cycle*: eleven of the seventeen nodes (R1 R2 R3 R3a R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 R16 R17) form one strongly connected component. So the cascade version is the wiring diagram cut at the tick: the edges that carry state into the *next* click become the click's initial haves, and what remains is one click's formation, acyclic, with its meets.

㊢ (what the cut exposes) I tried the obvious cut inline — the enactment edges `R16→R1/R2` (`u`, `world`), the belief recurrence `R3→R1` (`s-next`), the learned parameters `R4→{R1,R2,R3,R3a}` (`A`,`B`), and the fit/precision feedbacks. Two small cycles remain: `R6⇄R17` (`pi` out, `E` back) and `R4⇄R7` (`A` out, `rates` back). Both are the same thing: one box holding two units. R6 is both *candidate action space* (produces π) and *selection* (needs G); R4 is both *forward model* and *the model whose parameters precision-estimation reads*. The figure can draw that as one box with arrows in and out; a cascade cannot, and splitting them is the simplification doing its work rather than a defect. With the eleven cuts in place, the remaining order already has 36 meets, among them `R19 ⊓ CTAU-TOKEN = R5`, `R1 ⊓ R19 = R5`, `R2 ⊓ R13 = R4`, `R13 ⊓ R14 = R6`: R5 is the meet of preference and prediction — G is the emergent structure of that square, which is your diamond-is-a-pattern point on the R-nodes themselves.

🈖 ("a simplification of the elaborated wiring diagram") What goes, and where it goes: the five stage columns become a receipt field (they are one coarse *parse* — perceive, believe, evaluate, select, act is the recipe, not the formation); the Lean modules per node and the consumer binders become the unit's `:source`; the edge class is kept, because it matters: an `:absent` edge is drawn precedence with no term carried in Lean, which in `ConstructionReceipt` terms is an edge whose token set is empty — `valid` would reject it exactly as it rejects the forged chain edge. Ten of the forty-three are in that class (all seven `R4→…` edges among them). So the cascade version of the figure would show, as a property of the order, which of the drawn dependencies the Lean model actually carries.

㊭ (project, as checks) 1. A script beside `harness-figure.bb`, reading the same three p4ng files, that writes `r-cascade.edn`: units with modules, descent edges with token sets and class, the cut (each cut edge named with the reason: cross-tick state / learned parameter / split unit), the meets, the linear-extension count, and the `ConstructionReceipt` projection with absent-class edges flagged. 2. A drawing of it as a Hasse diagram or S-expression, not columns. 3. The Lean receipt for the result, as for the outer diamond. 4. Later, the comparison with the catalogue's Pattern map and the apparatus flexiargs, so each R-unit's IF/HOWEVER/THEN is read against its in- and out-tokens.

🈯 (the one design choice) The cut is the only non-mechanical step: where the click begins and ends, and whether R6 and R4 are split. I will propose a cut in the discovery report with each cut edge justified from the term it carries, and you rule on it there rather than in the abstract. I'll dispatch item 1 to codex-33 when check 4 returns (it is running now, job `invoke-1791240428501-33237-e9e4c29a`), unless you'd rather it went to a second seat in parallel.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("each pattern is itself a tiny diamond") Written as a table in §2a: IF/context = the generic space and the tokens accepted; HOWEVER = the two input spaces, the forces in conflict; THEN = the blend, whose emergent structure is the held tension (an alcove is neither the family room nor a private room) and the token emitted (is / is not an ALCOVE); BECAUSE = why the square commutes, the pattern's own structural equation that `k-unmet = k-if ∧ ¬k-then` abstracts. IF on top, two forces incomparable, THEN their meet — so a pattern is a blend square and a four-node semilattice at once, and a cascade is diamonds pasted along tokens, the same shape at two grains.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("lots and lots of ALCOVEs … not actually be that nice") In claude-17's terms that is the *other* off-diagonal: `IF ∧ ¬THEN` is a problem unaddressed, which he counts; `¬IF ∧ THEN` is a solution without its problem, which nobody counts. A per-step C that credits tokens held rewards exactly this (it is §5's bag problem at the grain of one pattern); the token story handles it the way v2 handles a missing edge — an emitted token with no consuming want earns nothing. Both off-diagonals should cost; today only one does.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("we could probably say … restate it as a design pattern") The outer-loop diamond is the instance: IF = `observe`; HOWEVER = ordinary work against self-repair, which is word for word `injury`'s HOWEVER ("merely adding a large penalty to M/E/T leaves unsafe acts in support … treating every failure as injury creates a self-repair dark room"); THEN = `minimise`; BECAUSE = G is defined over policies with predicted consequences. A complete flexiarg, `meta/select-the-meta-item`, drafted in the note and not put in the library — that is yours.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("additional requirements" / "better structure") My reading, in §5a: two moves on the diagram. An additional requirement pastes in a new square (new want token, new input space); better structure replaces a blend by one higher in Goguen's quality order over the same inputs — the 3/2-pushout is the maximum among consistent cones, refinement is movement toward it, and a living object (Crumb's crossroads) is one whose inputs also move, so the maximum moves. First classification of our own record: 09-15 → v2 and v2 → v3 are better structure over the same wants; Q1–Q10 and the pattern-graph diff were additional requirements. Checkable against the spec history, after the §6 items.
